lines.text: a matter of course: we feel immediate sympathy with
the Publican in his modesty and humility, whilst the
Pharisee in his self-conscious pride is so repulsive to us that
we are almost tempted to say: "I thank Thee, God, that I
am not as this Pharisee!"
But if we were to speak thus we should have misunder-
stood the story. We should not in any case have rightly
understood it as a message addressed to ourselves. It is
dangerous if it appears to us as something completely self-
explanatory. We must not forget that when the story was
narrated it seemed to the average listener at least to be
obnoxious and offensive. They felt it as a defiant and
offensive thing that the exemplary Pharisee, who represented
a generally respected class of men, and who was irreproach-
able, should have been put to shame thus by being contrasted
with the Publican, who belonged to a class that was despised
and avoided, a class with which no self-respecting man could
have anything to do. We need only consider what our
reaction would be if we ourselves, who perhaps do not feel
ourselves to be particularly distinguished examples of our
profession and status, but are nevertheless proud that we do
belong to a respected class and follow an honourable calling
in life—if we were similarly put to shame by being con-
trasted with the example of a man who came from the most
degraded and shunned sections of the community, from
which only what was squalid and vulgar could be expected.
In any case if the story does not strike us too as offensive and
obnoxious, as it struck its first hearers; if we do not feel that
we are perhaps intended by the Pharisee; then it is to be
feared that we have not rightly understood it, and listened
to it.
We are certainly quite right in being careful to see that
in our circle and profession, propriety and decorum and a
good moral tone should be a matter of course; and it is
assuredly legitimate for a man to be proud of his station in
life, whatever it be, proud of his rank and profession and of
the respect which accrues to it through conscientiousness and
